question: What is the smallest positive perfect cube that can be written as the sum of five consecutive integers?
explanation: Sum of five consecutive integers can be written as <math><mo>(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>k</mi></math>, so the sum must be a multiple of 5. If <math><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> equals this sum, then 5 divides <math><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math>, hence 5 divides <math><mi>m</mi></math>. Write <math><mi>m</mi>=<mn>5</mn><mi>t</mi></math>, so <math><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>3</mn></msup>=<mn>125</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math>. The smallest positive choice is <math><mn>125</mn></math> (take <math><mi>t</mi>=<mn>1</mn></math>). This gives <math><mi>k</mi>=125/5=<mn>25</mn></math>, and the five integers are <math><mn>23</mn></math>, <math><mn>24</mn></math>, <math><mn>25</mn></math>, <math><mn>26</mn></math>, <math><mn>27</mn></math>, whose sum is <math><mn>125</mn></math>.
derivation_summary: Sum = 5k; any cube equal to the sum must be divisible by 5, so its base is divisible by 5. Smallest base 5 gives 5^3 = 125, with k = 25 and consecutive integers 23–27.
